capture.final_message:
View `Module.piEquiv v` as the linear-combination map
\[
w \longmapsto \sum_i w_i\smul v_i.
\]

First establish this evaluation formula for a `Fintype ι`; this is exactly the second conjunct. Then show that the range of this linear map is precisely `Submodule.span R (Set.range v)`: every output is a linear combination of the `v i`, while each `v i` is obtained using the coordinate function supported at `i`.

Finally use `LinearMap.surjective_iff_range_eq_top` to convert surjectivity into
\[
\operatorname{span}_R(\operatorname{range} v)=\top.
\]
For the first conjunct, obtain a noncomputable `Fintype` from the assumed `Finite ι`. Finiteness is essential because arbitrary coefficient functions represent finite linear combinations only when the index type is finite.
